note: After the revision by Constantino (1995), the original in English. The soldier and worker are described, the alate being recorded in the original as unknown (Imago. Unknown.). Soldier measurements: 5 soldiers from 4 colonies, head length 4.50—4.80 mm, maximum head width 3.55—3.80 mm, head height without postmentum 2.25—2.40 mm, frontal tube length 0.17—0.22 mm, left mandible length 2.20—2.35 mm, left mandible M1—M2 distance 0.50—0.60 mm, left mandible width 0.60—0.64 mm; large worker measurements: 5 individuals from 4 colonies, head length 2.50—2.65 mm, maximum head width 2.90—3.15 mm, pronotum width 1.55—1.80 mm, metanotum width 1.55—1.85 mm, hind tibia length 3.65—4.05 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is characterised by an elongate head with parallel sides, weak thoracic spines situated anteriorly, and well-developed marginal teeth on both mandibles. S. longiceps is superficially similar but has only 19-segmented antennae, stouter mandibles with smaller marginal teeth, larger thoracic spines, and a completely different geographical distribution.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule elongate, sides parallel; posterior margin of the head rounded. Frontal tube projecting, sometimes set in a small depression; its aperture not visible in dorsal view. Labrum moderately elongate; lateral corners of the labrum about right-angled; median lobe elongate, longer than the lateral lobes. Antennae 20 or 21-segmented. Postmentum as described in the original.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker: head capsule with many short, straight setae; postclypeus with 4 setae; fontanelle small and slightly elongate. Antennae 20 or 21-segmented. Lateral margins of the thoracic tergites angular but without distinct spines. Molar plate of the mandibles narrow, the basal notch about 90°. Hindgut similar to that of S. dirus.
